questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was supposed to go to California but that fell through partly due to COVID, so my focus became solely on a place not too far away with a good academic reputation. Bergen fit that mold.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a good experience overall

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There is a big student center where you can easily get help. Writing over e-mail was a bit frustrating since the response was slow but upon arrival, it was pretty smooth to just seek help in person.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I got help with transport card for students, gym and overall mental wellbeing.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Pretty good. Again, everything was available at the student center.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Pretty easy! Just go to
hybel.no
or look at different facebook groups. Plenty of rooms available. I found something in the city center for a decent price.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: The student housing through the uni is extremely competitive so I wouldnt even waste time on it. Find it on your own. Its easy and fast.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The prices for student housing were good but it is extremely competitive so it seemed impossible. You had to be really lucky unless you wanted to live far from the city.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I got help from Toril Salen with the courses.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I found the courses I wanted on the website and wrote to Toril since the courses were masters level and im undergraduate student.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Toril was able to get me the courses I wanted.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got everything I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Go after the courses you want! Even if they arent on your level, you might get lucky like I was.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was great. Good lectures.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Mostly masters and one undergraduate.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had more classes but the level seemed about the same. More social since we had to interact more and do group work at almost all classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Pedagogiske perspektiv på læring
Psykologisk Kartlegging
Psykologisk Behandling

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them were great.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Everything was MUCH more expensive than back home. Norway is very expensive so bring more money than you expect to use!

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything was more expensive. Going out to eat or have a drink was crazy expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Bergen has lots of cultural offers for students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Concerts, events, talks, group hiking, movie clubs etc

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Bergen is a very beautiful city so I would recommend exploring by foot. Also all the cultural events.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Take the fløyen, ulrikke, KODA museum

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very. Norway and Denmark is quite similar in culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Norwegians are much more open than Danes in my experience, especially if they know you arent a local, so I would just say be open and speak to people! They will probably come to you too.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How open people were. I also appreciate that the language was similar to Danish so I could take classes in Norwegian!

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Bring more money than you expect! 2) Take advantage of all the beautiful sites not just in Bergen but other cities! 3) People are really friendly, so if you show interest in them, you can really get to know lots of people

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met and also getting insight into how they view psychology in Norway.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I did feel lonely at times, but that was my own fault.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO! Being on exchange has been great overall. Learning to be more independent and gaining insight into a different culture is always a good thing.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
